root_idea.summary: The root centers on smallness and lowliness, with tiny insects serving as a salient image.
root_idea.development: The lexical development connects small insects with contemptible or diminutive descriptions and with أَقْمَلَ, used of the rimth plant when it puts forth small leaves likened to those insects.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed as the Quranic noun قُمَّل, normalized from the inflected occurrence form.

senses.definition: Small flies or other tiny pests; the pest named in the Quranic occurrence and conventionally rendered “lice.”
senses.usage_conditions: Occurs in 7:133 as وَالْقُمَّلَ. Classical lexical identification is not uniform: it is described as small flies, while the supplied contextual rendering is “the lice.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small pest, identified as a kind of woodworm or as a type of tick.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical Arabic identification of the noun; it is kept distinct from the Quran-attested description of the occurrence as small flies.
A separate nominal form from قُمَّل.
A descriptive adjective, illustrated in the expression رَجُلٌ قَمِلٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Small and ugly, likened to a louse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A feminine descriptive form explicitly applied to a woman in the cited usage.
Attested as an epithet for a man in the expression رَجُلٌ قَمَلِيٌّ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of the rimth plant, to put forth small leaves.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized usage said of الرِّمْث; the small leaves are likened to قُمَّل.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Pointer-only cross-reference to تِينٌ; no lexical definition is supplied in the unit.
Pointer-only reference to حَنَطَ; the unit gives no semantic gloss for أَقْمَلَ.
Directly gives the classical insect or tick identification of قُمَّل.
Pointer-only cross-reference to تِينٌ; no lexical definition is supplied in the unit.

cautions: The exact zoological identification of قُمَّل is uncertain across the supplied evidence: it is described as small flies, conventionally rendered as lice, and elsewhere identified as a small pest or type of tick.
